text: When a transposed FIR on xc7s50 is DSP-timing-limited (critical path in DSP48E1 at 495 MHz) but uses 45 DSPs, avoid switching to symmetric fold=2 with in_pipe_out DSP registers and acc_width=38, as it reduces DSPs to 16 but moves the critical path to a 4-cell fabric carry chain (out_data_reg), collapsing fmax to 163 MHz (-332.5 MHz) because the symmetric accumulation forces a wide post-adder into fabric.

When a symmetric fold=2 FIR on xc7s50 is over an 8-DSP budget because acc_in_dsp=true spends 16 DSP48E1s, set acc_in_dsp=false to force one DSP48E1 per multiplier (8 DSPs) and move accumulation into fabric CARRY4, accepting a ~13 MHz Fmax loss (163.05 to 150.04 MHz) and +618 LUTs as the fabric carry-chain accumulator becomes critical.

When a symmetric folded FIR on XC7S50 is timing-limited by a fabric carry-chain partial-sum combine, increase the fold from 2 to 4 and enable acc_in_dsp to combine 4 partials in the DSP cascade, raising Fmax from 150.04 to 236.57 MHz (+86.5) and cutting LUTs from 1185 to 360 at 0.25 samples/cycle while holding 8 DSPs.

When a symmetric folded FIR on XC7S50 at fold=4 misses 250 MHz (236.6 MHz) with a route-dominated tap-operand mux/partial-sum critical path, doubling fold to 8 to halve the mux to 2:1 and cut DSPs 8→4 reduced LUTs by 95 but worsened Fmax to 225.5 MHz (-11 MHz) and path delay 3.87→4.12 ns, so do not raise fold to shrink mux depth when routing/combine dominates.

When an xc7s50 symmetric folded FIR is routing-limited by the tap-operand mux at 225.53 MHz, do not halve the fold from 8 to 4 and drop the DSP M pipeline (in_pipe_out→in_out), because it adds 4 DSP48E1s and 60 LUTs and drops Fmax to 152.07 MHz by worsening the same LUT6-to-LUT2 mux/coefficient routing congestion.

When a folded symmetric FIR on XC7S50 misses timing through a routing-heavy tap-operand mux and x[k]+x[N-1-k] pre-adder into the DSP input at fold=4, go non-symmetric fold=8 with acc_width 38->37 and in_out->in_pipe_out DSP registers to remove the pre-adder from that path while keeping 8 DSPs, raising Fmax 152.07->259.07 MHz (+107 MHz) with LUT 325->324.

When an xc7s50 FIR at fold=1, acc_in_dsp=true, transposed form violates DSP budget (45 DSP vs 8) while its 0.53 ns DSP48E1 M->P path gives ~495 MHz, move to symmetric fold=4 with acc_width=38, reg_in=true, DSP in_pipe_out, and acc_in_dsp=false: DSP falls 45->4 but LUT rises 1->632 and fmax falls 495.54->232.23 MHz because the critical path shifts from the DSP M->P register to the fabric 8:1 tap mux/partial-sum combine.

When a folded symmetric FIR on xc7s50 is timing-limited at 232.23 MHz by tap-mux routing, do not drop symmetry and reduce acc_width 38→37 at fold=4, because it doubles DSPs 4→8 and LUTs 632→1040 while collapsing Fmax to 157.13 MHz by moving the critical path to the FDRE→LUT3→carry-chain out_data path (6.34 ns).

When an XC7S50 DSP-registered FIR folded at 4 is timing-limited by a 6.34 ns carry-chain partial-sum path (157.1 MHz), use a pre-adder-free fold=8 and push the partial-sum accumulate back into fabric (4 DSP48E1s, U=32/F=8) to cut the critical path to 3.91 ns and raise Fmax to 238.3 MHz (+81.2 MHz, -449 LUT, -4 DSP), though it still misses 250 MHz.

When a folded FIR on XC7S50 fails timing/sim at 238.32 MHz with the critical path running from DSP48E1 m_q through a LUT2 into a 7-cell carry-chain on part_reg, move the accumulation into the DSP48E1 (acc_in_dsp=true) to eliminate that carry chain, reaching 259.07 MHz (+20.8 MHz) at 8 DSP48E1s and 324 LUTs.

When a folded FIR on XC7S50 is feasible at 259 MHz with 8 DSPs and a pure DSP48E1 M->P critical path, do not switch to symmetric fold=4 with a 38-bit accumulator: the added LUT6/LUT2 partial-sum combine routing (1.16 ns + 0.82 ns) moves the critical path off the DSP and drops Fmax to 236.6 MHz at the same 8-DSP count, losing feasibility.

On a 32-tap xc7s50 FIR that is DSP-resource-limited (45 DSPs vs an 8-DSP cap) while the DSP path is fast (495 MHz), only switch to fold=2, symmetric, registered-DSP-I/O, acc_in_dsp=false with a 38-bit accumulator if the DSP cap dominates: it drops DSPs to 8 but adds 1186 LUTs and collapses Fmax to 154 MHz because the critical path becomes the fabric tap-mux/accumulator carry chain.

When a folded symmetric FIR on XC7S50 is stuck at 154 MHz by a fabric carry-chain partial-sum combine at the 8-DSP cap, repartition to asymmetric fold=8 with acc_in_dsp=true, in_pipe_out DSP registers, and a 37-bit accumulator so accumulation moves inside the DSP48E1, raising Fmax to 259 MHz (+104.9 MHz) and cutting 863 LUTs at the same 8 DSPs (at 0.125 samples/cycle throughput).

When an XC7S50 folded FIR is already feasible at 259 MHz with the DSP input fully registered, do not add a fabric register after the multiplier to isolate the partial-sum-combine route: it creates an FDRE→DSP48E1 acc_n critical path of 4.16 ns and cuts Fmax by 35.6 MHz to 223.51 MHz (+36 LUT, same 8 DSP), losing feasibility.

When a folded symmetric FIR on XC7S50 at fold=4 with acc_in_dsp=true and pipe_mul=1 is timing-limited by a fabric partial-sum register launching into the DSP48E1 post-adder (223.51 MHz, 8 DSP, 4.16 ns path), move accumulation out of the DSP into fabric CARRY4 with acc_in_dsp=false/pipe_mul=0, which removed the DSP post-adder from the path and gave +8.7 MHz (232.23 MHz) and 8→4 DSP for +272 LUTs (632), though it still misses 250 MHz.

For a folded symmetric FIR on XC7S50 whose fold=4 critical path is dominated by the fabric tap mux and carry-chain partial-sum combine (232.2 MHz), set acc_in_dsp=true to keep the partials inside the DSP PCIN cascade; this cuts LUTs 632→360, adds 4 DSPs (4→8), and lifts Fmax only 4.3 MHz to 236.6 MHz because the remaining path is still LUT/routing, so it buys headroom but not 250 MHz feasibility.
